purpose: Universal inherited behavioural, evidence, contract, telemetry, inspection, test and security foundation for Alchemy ooRexx classes.

environment.validated_interpreter: Build validation: ooRexx 5.3.0 r13196 debug build using the live Security Manager semantics probe. Earlier project-host field evidence exists for the v0.4.3 lineage on ooRexx 5.2.0 r0; v0.8 requires its own field rerun before claiming release-level 5.2.0 validation.
environment.security_manager_profile: runtime-probed-reference-semantics (fail closed if live probe is unverified)

design_limitations: Static ::REQUIRES is not supervised by the per-routine Security Manager on the validated ooRexx 5.2.0 r0 and 5.3.0 r13196 builds.
Capability expiry uses local service wall-clock base-day and seconds-of-day values and therefore assumes sufficiently synchronized issuer/verifier clocks.
Pure-ooRexx cryptography is expensive for very large graph evidence; SOURCE/FULL embeds the concrete package source once and externalizes inherited dependency source by package identity.

Automatic method telemetry deliberately refuses PROTECTED, PRIVATE, PACKAGE-scope, and reserved AlchemyObject base-surface methods so instrumentation cannot weaken access, Security Manager checkpoints, or universal base behavior.

Automatic method telemetry now traps Rexx conditions through SIGNAL ON ANY, but abrupt process/interpreter termination can still leave a retained execution record incomplete rather than producing a normal exit classification.
FULL execution trace can disclose String argument values and requires its own TRACE:FULL capability.
Only explicitly registered object variables are exposed by the fixed state emitter; Clouseau probe inference remains separately capability/policy controlled.
Crypto-locked plaintext exists transiently in process memory while the operating Method executes; the service key-provider boundary must be chosen accordingly.
The included locked-method in-memory key provider is a reference/service-local implementation, not an HSM/KMS replacement.
The plaintext convenience builder must not be mistaken for at-rest secrecy when plaintext source literals are present in the same package SOURCE.
Direct use of Inspector Clouseau outside AlchemyInspectorBridge remains a separate authority surface and must be controlled by the hosted loader/policy.
Envelope subkey deletion is authoritative-provider revocation; it cannot erase raw key material that was previously exfiltrated.

The reference envelope provisioner derives keys deterministically from a 256-bit master because oorexx_crypto_v0.1 does not expose a dedicated cryptographic random-byte API; production may replace provisioning with HSM/KMS generation.

ooRexx does not provide a final-method declaration for this use; v0.5 detects descendant and object-specific shadowing of reserved AlchemyObject surfaces and rejects adoption rather than claiming language-level finality.

Adoption verification remains a point-in-time check; admission checkpoints can detect later reserved-surface drift when compared, but an unsealed checkpoint is evidence only and must not be treated as authority.

Execution provenance is automatic only for explicitly instrumented eligible methods; PROTECTED, PRIVATE, PACKAGE-scope and reserved AlchemyObject methods remain deliberately unwrapped so telemetry cannot weaken access or Security Manager semantics.

Execution provenance retains a bounded recent-history window (default 128 records, maximum configurable 4096); completed-record eviction and unretained active calls increment dropped_total rather than growing object memory without limit.
Execution records bind method contract identity/revision/fingerprint, implementation origin, entry integrity and result-contract outcome but deliberately do not copy raw argument or result values.

Implementation-origin attribution prefers exact effective Method-object identity; LINEAGE_DECLARATION_SCAN_FALLBACK is explicitly labelled when an interpreter does not preserve that identity through class introspection.

Cooperative method interposition is structural infrastructure cooperation, not an authority source; a host must trust the active coordinator implementation before treating coordinated execution provenance as high-assurance evidence.
